ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (New Zealand), as amended; Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), as amended; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; Privacy Act 2020; and the AML/CFT regulations and supervisory guidance issued by the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs and the Financial Markets Authority. Beneficial ownership information is collected and held by AML/CFT reporting entities and is accessible to supervisors and the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit upon lawful request; no public or government-only central UBO register is currently in force for New Zealand.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (of the corporate shareholder; and, after registration, of the New Zealand Limited)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry in the country of origin; for New Zealand, the New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize or certify in the issuing jurisdiction. If the issuing jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention state, obtain an apostille from that state's designated Competent Authority and do not seek consular legalization. If the issuing jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention state, follow the consular legalization chain through the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then the New Zealand Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain them.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Compliance Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office or the equivalent registrar in the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain the certificate from the relevant registrar. For destinations within the Apostille Convention, attach an apostille issued by New Zealand's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade or by the foreign jurisdiction's competent authority, respectively. For non-Apostille destinations, replace the apostille with foreign-ministry authentication followed by consular legalization by the destination state's consulate. Do not apply both processes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney executed by the beneficial owner and corporate director(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the ultimate corporate shareholder or the individual shareholder(s), notarized by a local notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize all signatures. If the place of execution is an Apostille Convention state, attach an apostille from that state's Competent Authority and forward it to New Zealand; no consular legalization should be added. If the place of execution is not an Apostille state, have the notarized document certified by the local Foreign Ministry and then legalized by the New Zealand Embassy or Consulate in that jurisdiction. The two paths are alternative and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Company Constitution (New Zealand equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office for the registered copy; the shareholder special resolution for adoption of the constitution; notarized certified copy for foreign use
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a New Zealand document used in a foreign jurisdiction, obtain a certified copy from the Companies Office, then if the destination is an Apostille member obtain a New Zealand apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade; if the destination is not an Apostille member, obtain MFAT authentication followed by destination-consulate legalization in New Zealand. For a foreign parent constitutional document entering New Zealand, use apostille or consular legalization in the parent's country only.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank in the country of origin where the beneficial owner or corporate shareholder maintains the account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank officer's signature must be notarized. If the bank's jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention state, attach an apostille from that jurisdiction's Competent Authority; if it is not an Apostille state, have the notarized letter certified by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then legalized by the New Zealand Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive; no sequential combination is permitted.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All named directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, authorized representatives, and anticipated counterparties must be screened before onboarding and on an ongoing, at-least-daily basis against the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, UK/EU financial sanctions lists, and adverse-media/Interpol sources. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any PEP match, high-risk jurisdiction, nominee relationship, or unusual payment-volume pattern associated with the video-match app or its Paymentwall and Apple IAP rails. Source of wealth and source of funds must be documented for every UBO; transaction and counterparty monitoring must be continuous; all screening evidence and risk ratings must be retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Company Name Reservation Portal (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Legal company names must be in Latin script. Chinese characters and other non-Latin scripts are not accepted as the statutory entity name; use an English or pinyin transliteration in the legal name, and consider registering the Chinese-character brand separately as a trademark. Te reo Maori names and words are permitted, but the statutory suffix must be Limited or Ltd. The recommended four-tier commercial naming convention is: distinctive brand element, business activity descriptor, geographic/strategic marker, and the mandatory Limited/Ltd suffix.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: During the initial 20-working-day reservation, apply before expiry for one further 20-working-day extension and pay the prescribed extension fee. If the Registrar rejects a proposed name, file a formal written objection through the Companies Office portal within 20 working days after the rejection, stating why the name is not false, misleading, or offensive, and attaching written consent from any regulator, statutory body, or prior rights holder whose approval is required. The Registrar must issue a written decision; if the refusal is maintained, the applicant may apply to the High Court of New Zealand for judicial review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office street address is acceptable to the Companies Office as a registered office only if it is a physical address in New Zealand, not a PO Box, and documents can be served at the address during normal business hours. For this specific medium-risk real-time video-matching app, however, New Zealand banks, Inland Revenue, and payment processors such as Paymentwall and Apple IAP merchant banks will require a demonstrable physical operating address, local management substance, business records, and meeting space. A virtual mailbox alone is not sufficient commercial substance and may trigger banking de-risking, enhanced IRD non-residence review, or payment-rail KYC failure

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand) sections 12-16 (registration and certificate of incorporation), sections 20-22 (constitution and company name), Part IV relating to share capital and allotment, Part VIII governing directors and duties, and sections 189 and 201 (registered office and address for service); Financial Reporting Act 2013 for financial reporting obligations
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company under section 13 of the Companies Act 1993, filed through the New Zealand Companies Office online register
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Companies Act 1993 prescribes no minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account rule. The company may be incorporated with nil issued capital and may allot no-par-value ordinary shares for such cash or non-cash consideration as the directors determine in accordance with Part IV of the Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA RESOLUTION OF FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [●] LIMITED (the 'Company'). AT the first meeting of the board of directors of the Company, duly convened and held on [date] at [time] at [place], the chairperson confirmed that a quorum was present and that all directors had received due notice of the meeting pursuant to the Company's constitution. After due deliberation and by unanimous consent, the following resolutions were proposed, seconded, and carried. 1. Share Capital Subscription. RESOLVED that the board adopt the initial ordinary share capital structure of the Company and approve the subscription by the subscribers of [number] ordinary shares with no par value at a consideration of NZ$[●] per share, or for such other lawful consideration, including cash, property, or services, as the board shall approve and record in the share register. RESOLVED FURTHER that the shares subscribed by each initial subscriber be allotted, that entry be made in the company's share register, and that definitive share certificates be issued under the hands of two directors or under the common seal of the Company if adopted. 2. Registered Office and Address for Service. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company shall be fixed at [street address, city, New Zealand], that the address for service in New Zealand shall be [service address, New Zealand], and that the Company shall file all requisite notices with the Registrar of Companies under sections 189 and 201 of the Companies Act 1993 to record the registered office and address for service. 3. Banking Authorities. RESOLVED that [bank name] at [branch address], New Zealand, be appointed as the principal banker of the Company; that operating, settlement, and treasury accounts be opened; and that the following persons, namely [names of officers], be and are hereby appointed as authorised signatories, acting jointly or severally in accordance with the approved mandate. RESOLVED FURTHER that the directors be authorised to execute the bank account opening documents, to establish online banking and wire transfer limits, and to revise the banking mandate by resolution of the board upon not less than two business days' notice to the bank. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. RESOLVED that [name] be and is hereby appointed as a director of the Company for the purposes of the Companies Act 1993, that [name] be and is hereby appointed as chairperson of the board, and that [name] be and is hereby appointed as corporate secretary and compliance officer with responsibility for maintaining statutory registers, filing annual returns, and coordinating AML/CFT obligations where applicable. RESOLVED FURTHER that every appointed officer shall hold office until death, resignation, or removal in accordance with the Company's constitution and the Companies Act 1993. 5. General Authority and Indemnity. RESOLVED that all directors and officers of the Company be and are hereby severally authorised to execute and deliver all agreements, instruments, and documents, and to take all such steps as may be necessary or desirable to implement the foregoing resolutions. RESOLVED that this meeting stands adjourned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and File Incorporation Application with the Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) via the online companies register at companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the New Zealand Companies Office online registry. Run a name availability search to confirm that the proposed name is not identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered name under the Companies Act 1993. Complete the online Application for Registration of a Company, inputting the proposed name, registered office address, address for service, full legal names, residential addresses, and dates of birth of all directors and shareholders. Attach a signed consent to appointment for each director and a signed copy of any constitution if adopted; if no constitution is filed, the default constitution in the Companies Act 1993 applies. Pay the official state filing fee by credit card or internet banking. Submit the application and retain the registration acknowledgement. Upon approval, the Registrar will issue the certificate of incorporation and the New Zealand Business Number.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and name approval search record
Full legal names, residential addresses, and dates of birth of directors and shareholders
Signed consent to appointment of each director
Registered office address and address for service in New Zealand
Constitution, if adopted, otherwise default constitution applies
Payment of official incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the application through a requisition, respond within the stated deadline through the online portal. If the name is rejected, file a revised name application or request reconsideration under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993. If identity verification is required, provide certified copies of passports or another acceptable government-issued identification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hold the First Board Meeting and Adopt Corporate Governance Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The board of directors of the company, administered by the corporate secretary or New Zealand legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following issue of the certificate of incorporation, the corporate secretary shall convene the first board meeting by written notice no fewer than five business days in advance. The chairperson shall confirm quorum and the validity of the meeting. The board shall adopt the pro-forma first board resolution covering the allocation and subscription of shares, adoption of the registered office, appointment of statutory officers, and authorisation of bank account arrangements. The secretary shall record the minutes, allot the shares, issue share certificates, and place the certificate of incorporation and constitution into the company minute book. All resolutions shall be signed by the chairperson and countersigned by the secretary. Executed bank account opening packets and authorised signatory forms shall be submitted to the selected bank in accordance with the banking resolution.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and New Zealand Business Number confirmation
Constitution as adopted
Notice of first board meeting and agenda
Pro-forma first board resolutions and executed minutes
Director and shareholder identification documents
Bank account opening forms and signatory mandate
Share certificates and share register entries
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any director consent is defective or a resolution is challenged, convene a new board meeting and adopt a ratifying resolution. If a statutory officer appointment is invalid, re-execute the consent and pass a fresh appointment resolution. If the error affects the public register, file a corrective notice with the Companies Office immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Verify and Complete Tax Registration with the Inland Revenue Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand, through the myIR secure online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, the company receives a New Zealand Business Number and an Inland Revenue Department number through the Companies Office and IRD data sharing process. The board shall verify receipt of the IRD number in myIR and complete a Goods and Services Tax registration application if the app revenue is expected to exceed NZ$60,000 in any twelve-month period. The company shall register for employer PAYE if it hires employees, register for resident withholding tax and fringe benefit tax where applicable, and appoint a tax agent if desired. All registrations shall be submitted through the myIR portal using the company's NZBN and IRD number. The compliance officer shall retain all confirmation receipts and maintain the company's tax master file records.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and NZBN confirmation
Board resolution authorising tax registrations
Director identification and IRD information if previously held
Business activity description and projected revenue
GST registration application where applicable
PAYE and fringe benefit tax registration forms where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD number or registration is delayed, contact the IRD business line with the NZBN, date of incorporation, and certificate of incorporation. Any late-filing penalty may be remitted under the Tax Administration Act 1994 if the failure is unintentional; a voluntary disclosure should be filed promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish Statutory Registers, Annual Return Calendar, and Continuing Compliance Files
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate secretary and compliance officer under the direction of the board of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish the company's statutory registers and compliance filings calendar. The secretary shall prepare and maintain the share register, director register, charges register, and register of interests using the forms required by the Companies Act 1993. The secretary shall set a filing calendar showing the annual return date, which is due within one month of each anniversary of incorporation, and the financial reporting obligations under the Financial Reporting Act 2013. The board shall confirm that the registered office and address for service are correct and that any changes are lodged on the proper Companies Office forms. If the company's business model falls within the New Zealand AML/CFT regime, the compliance officer shall establish the AML/CFT compliance programme and risk assessment in accordance with the company's enhanced risk rating. All records shall be made accessible for inspection at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and NZBN confirmation
IRD number confirmation and tax registrations
First board minutes and resolutions
Share register, director register, and charges register templates
AML/CFT risk assessment and compliance programme, if applicable
Annual return calendar and financial reporting framework election
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an annual return is past due, file it online immediately and pay any late fee. If a statutory register contains an error, apply to the Registrar of Companies for correction under section 210 of the Companies Act 1993. If AML/CFT obligations are uncertain, seek a supervisory assessment from the Department of Internal Affairs before commencing operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Inland Revenue) of New Zealand, operating through the myIR secure online portal and administered in coordination with the New Zealand Companies Office and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a New Zealand limited company: (i) Incorporate the company online through the New Zealand Companies Office under the Companies Act 1993; the system automatically issues the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). (ii) Apply to Inland Revenue for the company's IRD number using the prescribed non-resident company registration procedure lodged through myIR or the applicable Inland Revenue paper application; furnish the certificate of incorporation, NZBN, registered office address, director and ultimate beneficial owner details, and a valid street address for service both in New Zealand if a place of business exists and abroad if not. (iii) Concurrently or subsequently complete Goods and Services Tax (GST) registration in the same myIR account if the entity will carry on a taxable activity and annual taxable supplies exceed the statutory threshold, electing a GST filing frequency and an accounting basis that fits the cross-border digital services model. (iv) Maintain a New Zealand bank account or documented foreign currency settlement arrangement for GST refund and export substantiation purposes, and notify Inland Revenue within the statutory timeframe of any changes to directors, address, contact information, or cessation of the New Zealand taxable activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (a New Zealand limited company is a separate legal entity taxed at entity level on its worldwide income if incorporated in New Zealand, with branch equivalent rules applying to non-resident companies carrying on business in New Zealand; there is no pass-through classification for a standard NZ Ltd).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. New Zealand has no check-the-box or elective pass-through regime for limited companies; hybrid mismatch rules apply automatically under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018, and no statutory entity classification election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) levied under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies made in New Zealand over any 12-month period; the same NZD 60,000 threshold applies to non-resident suppliers of remote services to New Zealand resident customers, with voluntary registration permitted below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory digital stamping, or government pre-clearance requirement exists in New Zealand. Electronic invoicing is voluntary and operates on a PEPPOL-aligned interoperability framework; GST returns must be filed electronically through Inland Revenue's myIR portal, and GST liabilities are accounted for on the basis of the GST return periods rather than through a continuous fiscal clearance API.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of goods is zero-rated when the goods are physically exported from New Zealand by the supplier or on the supplier's behalf, and the supplier retains statutory evidence of export. A supply of cross-border services, including digital video matching and social telephony services, is zero-rated when the services are supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed and the services are not connected directly with New Zealand real property or with goods in New Zealand that are subsequently supplied to the recipient in New Zealand; services supplied remotely to New Zealand resident consumers are outside zero-rating and instead attract the standard 15% GST under the offshore remote services rules. The zero-rating claim must be supported by commercial, customs, and foreign exchange records sufficient to satisfy section 11 and related provisions of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 and Inland Revenue practice.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration lodged electronically through the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window in the approved export entry format
New Zealand Customs Service clearance/export certificate confirming the goods have left New Zealand
Bill of lading (sea freight) or airway bill (air freight) evidencing movement to the overseas destination
Original commercial invoice and packing list matching the export declaration

Foreign exchange repatriation evidence in the form of an inbound remittance advice, inward foreign currency transfer record, or bank statement identifying settlement of the export invoice from the overseas buyer's currency
Executed cross-border service agreement or user terms establishing the video matching services are delivered to non-resident users outside New Zealand
IP geolocation and server access logs substantiating the overseas use of the digital platform where zero-rated services are supplied
Certificate or statutory declaration where physical export documentation cannot be obtained, in accordance with Inland Revenue's acceptable evidence guidelines

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) - no separate foreign exchange administration; overseas investment screening is conducted by the Overseas Investment Office under the Overseas Investment Act 2005
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fully liberalised and open financial system with no foreign exchange controls or restrictions on current or capital account transactions. The New Zealand dollar is freely convertible and floats independently under a managed official cash rate framework operated by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand. There are no surrender requirements, no central bank approval for trade payments, no restrictions on the establishment of foreign currency bank accounts, and no dividend or profit remittance approval hurdles. New Zealand has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations and does not apply multiple currency practices. In practice, the only constraints arise from the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, which requires banks to conduct customer due diligence, beneficial ownership identification, and source-of-funds verification for cross-border payments. The Overseas Investment Act 2005 also imposes consent thresholds for acquisitions of sensitive land or significant business assets, but a standard non-resident equity subscription into an app developer company below those thresholds is unrestricted. Profit remittance to a non-resident shareholder is generally subject to non-resident withholding tax at treaty rates, but no foreign exchange conversion or Reserve Bank approval is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or conversion obligation exists under New Zealand law. Exporters may retain foreign currency receipts indefinitely in offshore or domestic foreign currency accounts. There is no mandated conversion timeline or minimum conversion ratio. Banks require accurate transaction details for Balance of Payments statistical reporting and AML/CFT record-keeping, and taxable income must be translated into New Zealand dollars for IRD filing using an acceptable exchange rate methodology.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Business Everyday/Current Account (NZD) and Foreign Currency Account (USD/AUD/EUR)
Business Main Account (NZD) and International Transaction Account (USD)
Business One Account (NZD) and Global Plus Foreign Currency Account
Business Transaction Account (NZD) and FXplus Foreign Currency Account
Business Account (NZD) and Foreign Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI providers are not statutorily prohibited in New Zealand and may be registered on the Financial Service Providers Register, but they are not licensed banks and cannot offer a fully regulated New Zealand dollar settlement account with a local branch number. For a medium-risk video-chat app with Apple IAP and Paymentwall payment rails, relying solely on a fintech EMI is assessed as medium-to-low viability. Mainstream banks require local domiciliation for GST/IRD reconciliation and Companies Office disclosure, and major clearing banks are better positioned to handle app-store merchant settlement and high-velocity cross-border receipts. The recommended structure is to use a tier-1 New Zealand bank as the treasury anchor and use EMI capabilities only as a supplementary collection gateway after the bank has approved the merchant-of-record model.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand AML/CFT law does not categorically mandate physical branch appearance. Banks may accept remote video verification with live photo identification, electronic risk assessment, and certified true copies of passports, particularly where directors are overseas. In practice, most tier-1 New Zealand banks require at least one statutory director or beneficial owner with a New Zealand connection to attend a video interview or be visited by an authorised representative. Remote consular proxy opening is generally accepted if the consular officer certifies identity and signature, but banks will typically reinforce this with an independent banker's reference and proof of registered address. A New Zealand tax resident director attending in person remains the fastest onboarding path; non-resident directors without existing New Zealand bank relationships should expect enhanced due diligence and additional evidentiary requests.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face onboarding of non-resident directors with no prior relationship to any New Zealand bank, combined with an equity injection whose source of wealth is unclear.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies; shareholder and director recent 12-month personal and/or corporate bank statements; tax residency certificates; professional accountant or solicitor letters confirming source of funds; curriculum vitae of each director; banker's reference from an existing regulated financial institution; statutory declaration of ultimate beneficial owners; share subscription agreement; and evidence that the inbound funds originate from a clearing bank account in the shareholder's own name.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership chain through an overseas holding company or trust where nominee directors or discretionary beneficiaries may conceal ultimate control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate registry extracts of every entity in the ownership chain; organisation chart; trust deed or register of trusts; memorandum and articles of the holding company; certified share register; director and shareholder identification; legal entity identifiers; independent negative media search reports; a written commercial rationale for the ownership structure; and signed declarations denying nominees or concealed beneficial ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Video-chat social app model is considered susceptible to fraudulent payment abuse, chargeback-related laundering, and third-party payment aggregation through app stores and virtual cards.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive corporate AML/CFT programme; user KYC and identity verification procedures; real-time transaction monitoring and sanctions screening system; device and behavioural analytics; geo-blocking policy for prohibited jurisdictions; chargeback policy and refund procedure; audited merchant-of-record agreements with Apple IAP and Paymentwall; evidence of segregated merchant settlement accounts; and a third-party independent security and AML audit report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered business scope under ISIC 6311 may be viewed as inconsistent with actual real-time video matching and cross-border social telephony, raising concerns of misrepresented business activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full product business plan; platform architecture and data flow diagrams; terms of service and privacy policy compliant with the Privacy Act 2020; target jurisdiction list; revenue and cost model; evidence that no statutory licence is required for the software service; board resolutions mapping treasury accounts to operational disbursements; projected cash flows showing app-store revenue settlement; corporate tax registration with IRD; and independent proof of substance such as office lease, registered address, staffing arrangements, and insurance policies.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity must be remitted via SWIFT MT103 from the overseas shareholder's regulated bank account to the New Zealand company's NZD clearing account at an RBNZ-registered bank. There is no Reserve Bank foreign exchange approval for ordinary share subscription, but the bank will require the beneficiary account name to match the registered company name, and the remittance instruction should state 'share subscription - [allottee name] - [share allotment reference]'. After receipt, the company must file a share allotment return with the New Zealand Companies Office. Treasury capital verification is supported by the bank credit entry, a director board resolution allotting shares, and a solicitor's confirmation. Source-of-funds documentation must be maintained for AML/CFT purposes. If the business is a sensitive industry or exceeds the applicable Overseas Investment Act threshold, an OIO consent application must be completed before settlement. For balance of payments statistical reporting, the payment purpose should be classified as equity capital investment rather than trade or services.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational trade and vendor payments should be executed via SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers, with MT202 COV used for interbank and correspondent settlement where required. For high-value infrastructure procurements, the company should use a commercial documentary letter of credit issued by the New Zealand bank and advised to the overseas beneficiary through SWIFT MT700, with reimbursement running under MT202/MT202 COV. For smaller and recurring disbursements such as content moderation, cloud hosting, and user refunds, documentary collections and corporate purchasing cards are acceptable, provided all underlying invoices are separately retained. Apple IAP and Paymentwall merchant settlements should be routed into the company's USD or NZD clearing account, then converted using pre-arranged FX facilities. Mirror account arrangements in USD, AUD, EUR, and GBP are recommended to reduce conversion costs and maintain liquidity buffers for foreign supplier payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts between NZD and USD, AUD, EUR, GBP, and CNH for committed revenue and cost exposures
FX swaps and rollover forward structures to manage working capital and settlement timing mismatches
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term intercompany shareholder loans and infrastructure financing
Vanilla FX options on NZD/USD and NZD/EUR for contingent royalty, licensing, or acquisition payments
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for counterparty currencies where local convertibility restrictions prevent physical settlement; NDFs are not required for NZD

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Companies Act 1993, s 213 and Companies Regulations 1994)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on the company's annual return date, being the anniversary of incorporation in each calendar year. The annual return must be filed online by the last day of the month containing that anniversary, unless the Registrar has approved a different annual return date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers a Registrar's notice under Companies Act 1993, s 318. If the company fails to remedy within 20 working days after notice, the company may be struck off the Companies Register and dissolved, with assets vesting in the Crown. Re-registration costs approximately NZ$500 (about US$310) and requires restoration proceedings before the Registrar or the Court.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: IR4 Company Income Tax Return and annual tax reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Inland Revenue Department (IRD / Te Tari Taake)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return must be filed by 7 July following balance date. Terminal tax on the preceding year's assessed liability is due 7 April. Non-standard balance date filings are adjusted to the corresponding dates under the Tax Administration Act 1994.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZ$250 immediately, with further monthly penalties for continuing default; late payment penalty of 1% on the first day, 4% on day 7, then repeated late payment penalties, plus statutory use-of-money interest on unpaid tax. Persistent non-filing leads to default tax assessments and debt collection, including bankruptcy or liquidation proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements prepared, signed and dated by directors (Companies Act 1993, s 201; Financial Reporting Act 2013)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Directors and shareholders; New Zealand Companies Office only for large companies and FMC reporting entities that are required to file financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be prepared within 5 months after balance date and, where an annual meeting is held, laid before the meeting; a shareholder written resolution may replace the meeting. A 31 March balance date therefore requires completion by 31 August.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to prepare and sign financial statements commit an infringement offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, with fines up to NZ$10,000 per director and possible director disqualification; failure to file when required as an FMC reporting entity carries continuing penalties of NZ$50 per day plus a maximum NZ$500,000 for serious non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory audit report where audit is mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; the auditor is an independent limited-service auditor registered with the New Zealand Companies Office / Financial Markets Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed and the signed audit report delivered to shareholders within the same 5-month financial statement window following balance date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor when shareholders have validly required one is a Companies Act offence. Carrying on business while disqualified from acting as an auditor is punishable by imprisonment of up to 6 months or a fine of up to NZ$15,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual share register / director register verification and notification of outstanding registry changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office; internal statutory registers maintained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Changes in directors, shareholders, registered office, and constitution must be notified within 20 working days of the change; the annual return cycle requires positive confirmation that those register entries are up to date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with change-notification obligations may result in an infringement notice fee of NZ$200 per offence under the Companies Act 1993; inaccurate register details may expose directors to fines of up to NZ$10,000 and strike-off exposure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent certified auditor is mandatory for: (1) every New Zealand FMC reporting entity unless specifically exempted by regulation; (2) every 'large company' under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, being a company that satisfies at least two of the following at balance date: total assets exceeding NZ$60 million, total revenue exceeding NZ$50 million, or 250 or more full-time equivalent employees; (3) any company whose shareholders holding not less than 5% of voting rights have requested an audit under Companies Act 1993, s 202; (4) any company whose constitution or stakeholder covenant (e.g., lender or investor agreement) expressly requires a CPA audit; and (5) a subsidiary company where the parent's consolidation audit needs NZ statutory accounts. For smaller companies, a balance-sheet total of NZ$5 million, annual turnover of NZ$10 million, or 50 employees are material indicators used to place the entity in the Tier 2 / SME financial reporting framework, but they do not, by themselves, trigger a statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP) as set by the External Reporting Board (XRB). Applicable framework: NZ IFRS (Tier 1 large and publicly accountable FMC entities); NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (Tier 2 non-publicly accountable for-profit entities); and NZ Financial Reporting Standards for SMEs / NZ IFRS for SMEs (Tier 3 and Tier 4 smaller companies). Cross-border app revenue through Apple IAP and Paymentwall must be recognised under NZ IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers and reflected in the company's annual tax reconciliation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a standalone public UBO registry for private limited companies. The annual return filed with the Companies Office constitutes the annual statutory confirmation that the register of directors, register of members, registered office, and significant control entries are accurate. Any transfer of shares must be recorded in the Register of Members as soon as practicable, and an allotment or change of directors must be delivered to the Registrar within 20 working days. Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT), if the company is a financial institution or reporting entity by virtue of the app's payment facilitation activities, it must identify and verify beneficial owners and update that information at least annually or upon triggering events. The medium-risk / Enhanced Due Diligence rating for the Real-Time Video Matching and Cross-Border Social Telephony business requires an enhanced ongoing EDD review of beneficial ownership at least once every 12 months.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders and share transfers, Companies Act 1993, Part 8)
Register of Directors (directorships, consents and addresses, Companies Act 1993, s 192)
Register of Charges (mortgages and security interests over corporate assets, Companies Act 1993, Part 8)
Minute Book (minutes of board and shareholder meetings and written resolutions, Companies Act 1993, s 189)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$150 - US$350 per year for a compliant registered office and corporate secretarial agent in New Zealand
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$6,000 - US$20,000 per year for a certified independent audit of a small-to-medium cross-border app company with payment rails through Apple IAP and Paymentwall

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% flat New Zealand corporate income tax rate, payable on the net taxable income of the New Zealand-resident company
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No free-zone, patent-box, or statutory tax-holiday regime is available in New Zealand. The principal effective incentives are: a 15% refundable R&D tax credit on eligible R&D expenditure, accelerated depreciation and timing deductions for eligible software development, unlimited loss carry-forward subject to the 49% shareholder continuity rule, and foreign tax credit relief under applicable double tax agreements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 company income tax return, filed electronically through the Inland Revenue myIR portal; larger companies may also be required to file the IR4J financial-statement supplement and Country-by-Country Reporting schedules where group revenue exceeds the statutory threshold.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return is due on 7 July immediately following the year-end. If a tax-agent extension is held, the return date is generally moved to 31 March of the following year. Non-standard balance dates use the corresponding statutory due date under the Tax Administration Act 1994, and provisional tax must be paid in instalments based on prior-year liability or estimated assessable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IRD number, legal entity name, balance date, accounting period, number of months, and New Zealand tax residence status of the company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An NZ-incorporated video-matching app entity is a New Zealand tax resident under ITA 2007 s YD 2 regardless of where shareholders are located. If a Double Tax Agreement tie-breaker attributes residence elsewhere, full transfer pricing, PE, and disclosure schedules still apply. The return must identify each non-resident director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner because the IRD will pierce through nominee arrangements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross business income before deductions, including all video-matching subscriptions, Apple IAP receipts, Paymentwall settlements, in-app advertising revenue, cross-border telephony charges, and ancillary data monetisation, reported in New Zealand dollars.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: New Zealand-source income must be separately declared, including amounts attributable to a New Zealand PE or to functions, assets, and risks located in New Zealand. Gross receipts must not be reduced by app-store commissions or payment-processor deductions; those amounts are treated as business expenses in Box 3, not as net revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses, including wages of New Zealand engineers and content moderators, cloud hosting, user acquisition, video bandwidth, royalties, interest, legal costs, and audit fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All related-party expenses must satisfy the arm's length standard under ITA 2007 s GC 14 and the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines. Intercompany royalties and management fees to associated offshore video-matching or payment-intermediary entities are deductible only where the recipient performs actual functions, assumes real risk, and receives economically appropriate consideration. Interest deductibility is further restricted by the non-resident thin-capitalisation debt-to-asset ratio of 60%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / Net taxable income or loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after all deductions, addbacks, depreciation, capital allowances, and offset of prior-year tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss offsets are available only if a 49% shareholder continuity is maintained from the loss year to the year of offset, under ITA 2007 s IA 5. Any issue of shares, reorganisation of the discretionary trust, or transfer of video-matching IP to a foreign parent can break continuity and quarantine past losses. A foreign-owned NZ company must compute 28% tax on the full Box 4 amount before any shareholder-level relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resident withholding tax credits, non-resident withholding tax credits, imputation credits, foreign tax credits, and R&D tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit-claiming for non-resident shareholders must be supported by a valid Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial-ownership statement. Foreign tax credits require calculation under the applicable DTA, with credit limitation based on New Zealand tax on the same income. If Apple IAP and Paymentwall revenue is booked through an offshore intermediary without economic substance, the credit claim will be rejected and the income reconstructed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Residual income tax and provisional tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax result equal to 28% of Box 4 less Box 5 tax credits, less provisional tax instalments already paid, resulting in tax payable or refund due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Residual income tax is the box used for cross-border debt enforcement. If unpaid residual tax exceeds the statutory threshold, a director or principal shareholder can be served with a Departure Prohibition Order preventing exit from New Zealand. Underpayment of provisional tax will also generate use-of-money interest, even if the final return is filed on time.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of all transactions with associated non-residents: platform royalties, technical fees, cost-sharing obligations, shareholder loans, dividend distributions, and Apple IAP/Paymentwall settlements routed through connected intermediaries.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The schedule is the first place the IRD looks for profit repatriation and TP exposure. A contemporaneous OECD-compliant local file should be attached showing the tested entity, transfer pricing method, comparability adjustments, financial ratios, and arm's length price. Failure to maintain and produce the documentation gives the Commissioner the right to reconstruct pricing adversely and to apply penalty percentages of up to 150%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the IR4 attracts a monthly late-filing penalty, daily use-of-money interest, and shortfall penalties under TAA 1994 s 141 of 20%, 40%, 75%, or 150% depending on whether the position is unreasonable, unacceptable, abusive, or evasive. Knowingly providing false information or evading tax is criminal under TAA 1994 ss 143A-143B and may expose a company to a fine of up to NZ$250,000 and directors to imprisonment for up to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The domestic statutory NRWT on outbound dividends is 30% of the gross dividend, payable before the dividend is remitted. The dividend-paying NZ company is the withholding agent and must deduct and return NRWT regardless of whether the shareholder is a direct foreign holder or an intermediary in the Apple IAP or Paymentwall payment collection chain. Imputed dividends, excessive shareholder loans, and artificial management fees can be recharacterised as dividends subject to this 30% rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident recipient must satisfy all of the following: (1) obtain an official Certificate of Tax Residence from the foreign revenue authority covering the relevant income year; (2) complete and submit an NRWT treaty-rate declaration in myIR attaching the certificate and evidencing beneficial ownership of the dividends, interest, or royalties; (3) provide legal ownership evidence, including share registers, trust deeds, nominee explanations, and board minutes showing the recipient is not a conduit or mere agent; (4) demonstrate that the Principal Purpose Test and any Limitation on Benefits article in the applicable DTA and OECD Multilateral Instrument are satisfied; and (5) retain all source documents for at least seven years. Treaty relief is not automatic; in the absence of the required filing, the default 30% dividend NRWT, 15% interest NRWT, or 15% royalty NRWT is assessed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: New Zealand statutory NRWT rates are 15% for outbound interest and 15% for outbound royalties, with certain listed-debt interest exempt if the Approved Issuer Levy is paid. Under the NZ-Australia and NZ-US double tax agreements treaty rates are commonly reduced to 10% for interest and 10% for royalties, with some US royalty categories reduced to 5%, and dividend rates generally reduced to 15%, subject to holding thresholds, beneficial ownership, and administrative relief procedures.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Zealand has no bright-line statutory NZD threshold requiring automatic Local File or Master File preparation, but any material cross-border related-party transaction must be supported by contemporaneous OECD transfer pricing documentation. Country-by-Country Reporting is mandatory for NZ constituent entities of multinational groups with consolidated group revenue above NZ$680 million; failure to file or produce supporting local files allows the IRD to draw adverse inferences and apply shortfall penalties at the top statutory range.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations law of the Cayman or BVI type, but the general anti-avoidance rule in ITA 2007 s BG 1, the commerciality rules, Part 6 thin-capitalisation legislation, and the OECD-aligned transfer pricing provisions require real economic substance. Core Income-Generating Activities for the video-matching app, including algorithm maintenance, content moderation, user revenue collection, and board control over risk and capital, must be performed by actual staff in New Zealand. If those CIGA functions are relocated to a low-tax offshore shell while the New Zealand entity retains only the risk of high-cost operations, the IRD will recast the arrangement, deny deductions, impose NRWT, and impose director liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The NZ company records excessive royalties and management fees to a related Hong Kong or Singapore video-matching intermediary that performs no unique functions, has no New Zealand economic substance, owns no valuable IP, and exists solely to receive Apple IAP and Paymentwall cash flows, leaving zero or negligible taxable profit in New Zealand while the overseas entity accumulates the true economic profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner may reconstruct the transaction at the arm's length amount under ITA 2007 ss GC 13-GC 15, impose mandatory use-of-money interest under TAA 1994 s 120, and apply a shortfall penalty under s 141 of up to 150% of the resulting tax shortfall. If the failure is deliberate, criminal prosecution under TAA 1994 s 143B may follow, with fines up to NZ$250,000 and imprisonment for up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil will be pierced under the Companies Act 1993 ss 300 and 301 where directors cause the company to trade recklessly or fraudulently by draining profits through non-arm's length intercompany charges. Directors may be personally ordered to repay dissipated company assets, disqualified from managing companies for up to five years, served with Departure Prohibition Orders that blacklist them from leaving New Zealand, and subjected to criminal imprisonment for intentionally falsified TP records.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: NRWT Evasion through Disguised Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The NZ Ltd labels outbound cash flows to non-resident shareholders as shareholder-loan repayments, cost reimbursements, or data-access fees even though no genuine loan documentation, market-rate interest, or arm's length service exists, thereby distributing accumulated video-matching earnings without deducting the statutory 30% dividend NRWT or the appropriate 15% interest/royalty NRWT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: NRWT is imposed under ITA 2007 Part 8, and the payer company is personally liable for any amount it fails to withhold under TAA 1994 s 31B and s 159. The unpaid tax is subject to UOMI, shortfall penalties up to 150%, and criminal evasion under s 143B. Similarly, false classification of revenue as debt repayment rather than dividend is an offence that carries fines up to NZ$250,000 and imprisonment for up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under TAA 1994 s 159, the duty to withhold is imposed on directors and officers in their personal capacity, so directors can be made personally liable for unrecovered NRWT, penalties, and interest without the need to lift the corporate veil. Courts may order asset restitution, issue departure prohibition orders preventing travel, and convict directors for knowingly filing false declarations with the Companies Office, resulting in imprisonment under the Companies Act 1993 s 382.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML-Backed Shell Company and Economic Substance Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The entity operates as a trust-protected shell with nominee shareholders, no physical New Zealand office, no board minutes, no independent CIGA records, hidden ultimate beneficial ownership, and no AML/CFT customer due diligence or suspicious-transaction reports for Paymentwall payouts to high-risk video-merchant locations, while the NZ entity claims deductions and treaty benefits as if it were the true economic operator.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 ss 43-47 requires identification of beneficial owners and suspicious-transaction reporting; serious contraventions expose a body corporate to civil penalties up to NZ$2 million and individuals to fines up to NZ$200,000 and imprisonment. False UBO and director information filed with the Companies Office is an offence under the Companies Act 1993 s 382, and the IRD may invoke ITA 2007 s BG 1 to void the corporate structure and reassess all income as that of the true economic owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors cannot rely on the corporate veil where the company is a mere facade for tax fraud: they can be ordered to compensate creditor losses for reckless or fraudulent trading, disqualified as directors, blacklisted on Departure Prohibition Orders preventing departure from New Zealand, personally fined under AML/CFT legislation, and sentenced to imprisonment for deliberately using shell structures, nominee shareholders, and undisclosed video-matching revenue flows to evade tax and hide the ultimate beneficiaries.
